questions.problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
questions.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j,k}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
